punchline: Years of chess make you a master, but in a job where you never see the result, the same repetition may only grow your confidence.
thirty_sec: The psychologist Robin Hogarth divides learning environments into two. In kind environments like chess, results come fast and honest, so experience makes you a master. In a doctor's or an investor's world, feedback comes months later, sometimes never. According to David Epstein, years there can raise confidence rather than accuracy. That is why gathering examples from other fields is valuable.
